documents: Möller et al. (2022) Deglaciation history and subsequent lake dynamics in the Siljan region, Earth Surf. Process. Landforms 47:3515–3545 (published paper, PDF)

entry.evidence: after which these are examined and reinterpreted in the light of the recent

steps.action: Frame the study as a re-examination of early views of the Siljan deglaciation and lake history using modern LiDAR data and dated sediments.
steps.quote: after which these are examined and reinterpreted in the light of the recent

steps.action: Review the rival published accounts: von Post's normal back-wasting ice margin followed by Baltic water, versus Halden's stagnant basin ice, interconnected ice-dammed lakes and delayed deglaciation; Nordell's active-ice view of the lateral channels.
steps.quote: Halden (1929, 1933, 1936) was of a completely different opinion

steps.action: Use the national 2 m LiDAR elevation model previously characterized by co-authors for Swedish Quaternary geomorphology.
steps.quote: provided the LiDAR data used in this study

steps.action: Build hill-shaded DSMs with several illuminations, manually map streamlined terrain and ribbed moraine (9180 features), and core peat bogs and Lake Orsasjön with Russian and UWITEC piston corers.
steps.quote: manual mapping of all streamlined terrain (drumlins, mega-scale glacial lineation) and ribbed moraine features were then carried out

steps.action: Obtain 42 AMS radiocarbon dates on terrestrial macrofossils, calibrate them with IntCal20 in OxCal, and build age-depth models with Clam.
steps.quote: A total of 42 radiocarbon dates were performed at the AMS Radiocarbon Dating Laboratory

steps.action: Infer ice flow from the NNW under wet-based conditions from drumlin orientation and remoulded ribbed moraine; infer vertical ice thinning and separation of dome and basin ice from the gradients and cross-cutting of meltwater channels in the Nittsjö area.
steps.quote: These gradient relations demonstrate the gradual flattening of the ice surface profile as ice thinned with time.

steps.action: Check the deglaciation pattern in a second area, the Klikthed–Grunuberg drainage corridor, where erosion, braidplain and esker zones show stagnant ice in depressions and thick basin ice.
steps.quote: The Klikthed–Grunuberg glaciofluvial drainage zone (one of several such) is a good example for demonstrating the deglaciation dynamics

steps.action: Reject Halden's interconnected high ice-lateral lakes: his shoreline indicators are reinterpreted as ice-marginal drainage channels, and the local ice-dammed lakes were not interconnected.
steps.quote: are in fact ice-marginal drainage channels

steps.action: Reconstruct the 245 m Skattungen–Ore ice-dammed lake from shore scarps, deltas and terraces, together with its spillway through the Ockran–Born Valley and its sediment threshold (Skattungby Field).
steps.quote: A reconstruction of the areal extent of this lake shows dimensions of about 25 km in length

steps.action: Identify the highest shoreline indicators (beach scarps, ridges, deltas) at 37 sites around the Siljan and Orsasjön basins on the DSMs.
steps.quote: 37 sites are listed in Table S1 and plotted to their positions in Figure 8(a)

steps.action: Project all highest-shoreline data onto a N–S baseline and fit a gradient of 2.75 m/10 km with scatter within ±3 m, implying E–W isobases.
steps.quote: This gives a south to north gradient that rises 2.75 m/10 km

steps.action: Compare the fitted gradient with Halden's 2.8 m/10 km, which it matches, and with von Post's 9 m/10 km, judged unreasonably high; judge Halden's isobase directions an overinterpretation.
steps.quote: Our data confirms the findings of Halden (1936)

steps.action: Derive the expected deglaciation time of central Orsasjön under continued 350 m/yr retreat (no delay): c. 10,560 cal. BP.
steps.quote: the ice margin should have reached the central part of the Orsasjön Basin (48 km towards the NNW) in about 140 years

steps.action: Date the Or_2 core (8 dates plus at least 315 varves) to a minimum deglaciation age of c. 9800 cal. BP, and the slumped Or_5 core to maximum ages of 10,900–10,000 cal. BP.
steps.quote: which yields a minimum deglaciation age of c. 9800 cal.

steps.action: Combine the two Orsasjön records with independent basal dates from the Indor Valley and Spjutmo and with OSL dune ages, which converge on deglaciation at c. 10,500 cal. BP.
steps.quote: In summary, our radiocarbon dates of basal lake sediments within and around the Orsasjön Basin suggest a deglaciation at around 10,500 cal.

steps.action: Exclude Halden's (and partly Nordell's) delayed deglaciation with a lingering stagnant ice mass in the basins.
steps.quote: There is therefore no evidence of a ‘delayed’ deglaciation and the dwelling of a stagnated ice mass in the Siljan Basin

steps.action: Keep von Post's active NW recession with a subaqueous margin and simultaneous Baltic ingression, with a slightly diachronous highest shoreline.
steps.quote: Von Post’s (1934) original view thus still seems to hold true in its principles

steps.action: Pose the question of when the Siljan Basin became isolated from the Baltic, against the common assumption that it did so during the Ancylus stage.
steps.quote: To solve the long-standing question of when the Siljan Basin became isolated

steps.action: Design a basin-isolation study at Kollsjömyran (threshold 176 m), chosen near the Åkerö Channel and placed by the isobase geometry so that it isolates just before the Siljan Basin.
steps.quote: we conducted a basin-isolation study north of, but as close as possible, to the Åkerö Channel

steps.action: Core and date Kollsjömyran; reject the reversed unit-1 ages as root contamination and set Siljan Basin isolation at 9800 cal. BP, during the Initial Littorina Sea stage.
steps.quote: we set the age of the isolation of the Siljan Basin to 9800 cal.

steps.action: Compare the implied uplift rate (3.5 m/100 yr) with Gästrikland (6.3 m/100 yr) and explain the mismatch by auxiliaries (earlier deglaciation there; the slowed Ancylus regression) rather than revising the isolation age.
steps.quote: This anomaly is most likely related to the fact that Gästrikland was deglaciated earlier than the Siljan region

steps.action: Take up von Post's 'Åkerö catastrophe': a sudden 6–7 m lake lowering and outlet rerouting, dated by pollen to the Littorina maximum.
steps.quote: argued for a dramatic lake-level lowering event (the Åkerö catastrophe)

steps.action: Re-investigate the Åkerö and Heden sites to confirm or reject the catastrophic event and date the rerouting.
steps.quote: to confirm or reject the existence of a catastrophic drainage event

steps.action: Core the Åkerö Channel, date seven macrofossil samples (excluding one young contaminated date), and estimate a minimum abandonment age of c. 8500 cal. BP from the sand-to-gyttja transition.
steps.quote: the onset of limnic deposition (base of unit 2) took place at around 8,500 cal.

steps.action: Check the Åkerö ages against three dates from a reconnaissance core taken a year earlier about 5 m away.
steps.quote: reconnaissance core taken 1 year earlier, displaying the same age range

steps.action: Core and date the Heden Basin, exclude reversed basal dates, and identify a minerogenic-input anomaly (XRF, magnetic susceptibility, C/N) at 680–665 cm, dated 8800–8650 cal. BP, as erosion after lake lowering.
steps.quote: this inferred erosional event took place between 8800–8650 cal.

steps.action: Check the Heden event against the independent Åkerö minimum age; in the Appendix, use unaltered C/N ratios to rule out terrestrial detritus redeposition as the cause of the anomaly.
steps.quote: which is in general agreement with the minimum age of c. 8500 cal.

steps.action: Propose that a stochastic high-water event (e.g., a strong snow-melt season), rather than a specific climatic event, triggered the overflow and new outlet.
steps.quote: we rather propose that it resulted from stochastic climate variability

steps.action: Refine von Post's drainage scenario into a gradual rerouting over about 300 years (8800–8500 cal. BP), consistent with the absence of lower shore marks.
steps.quote: we see a more plausible, slower-acting scenario for this event

steps.action: Take up the long-standing interpretation of the Bonäs Line as a wave-cut palaeo-shoreline (De Geer, Högbom, von Post, Halden, Wenner & Lannerbro).
steps.quote: interpreted by him as a palaeo-shoreline

steps.action: Construct 26 W–E LiDAR cross profiles across the outermost Bonäs dunes and measure the dune-foot and beach-scarp break points.
steps.quote: We constructed 26 about W–E-directed and up to 1400 m long cross profiles

steps.action: Regress dune-foot altitudes (1.5 m/km, R = 0.459) and beach-scarp bases (0.208 m/km, R = 0.230) against distance.
steps.quote: Regression analysis results in a N–S gradient of about 1.5 m per kilometre

steps.action: Exclude the isochronous erosional shoreline: the large short-distance variance and an implied lake level of about 100 m at Leksand contradict it; the match of the beach-scarp gradient is judged coincidence; the line is instead read as the distal front of migrating dunes.
steps.quote: being formed as an erosional feature cutting into distal Mora Delta sediment, as argued by von Post (1934)

steps.action: Summarize the kept history: active ice recession, deglaciation c. 10,700–10,500 cal. BP, isolation c. 9800 cal. BP, Ancient Lake Siljan at 168–169 m, gradual rerouting from 8800 cal. BP, and the Bonäs Line as a dune front.
steps.quote: we find no support for the Halden view on ice stagnation and time-delayed deglaciation of these basins

Partly: independent cores and sites agree; no sensitivity tests of the age models

end.claim: Ice receded actively NW across the Siljan–Orsasjön Basin c. 10,700–10,500 cal. BP followed by Ancylus ingression; the basin isolated c. 9800 cal. BP; Ancient Lake Siljan (168–169 m) drained through Åkerö until a gradual rerouting c. 8800–8500 cal. BP; the Bonäs Line is a dune front, not a shoreline.

decisive_move.sentence: The radiocarbon and varve chronologies from the Orsasjön, Kollsjömyran, Åkerö and Heden cores supplied the timing that excluded Halden's delayed deglaciation and redated and slowed von Post's drainage event.

gates.evidence: The Kollsjömyran site was chosen to test the isolation timing, and the Åkerö/Heden re-coring was done to confirm or reject von Post's catastrophe (pp. 3534–3535); the LiDAR mapping was not hypothesis-directed. The chronology could have shown a delayed deglaciation, and the Bonäs regression could have shown a consistent shoreline, but interpretations remain qualitative. No analysis or threshold was fixed in advance.

imports.item: AMS radiocarbon dating with OxCal/IntCal20 calibration
Python Numpy and Pandas for morphometric statistics
Linear regression with Pearson's R for dune-foot and beach-scarp altitudes

novelty_claims.quote: Our LiDAR-based DSMs provide unprecedented insights into geomorphlogical details
has remained poorly constrained until now
the new chronological framework set up for this event suggests that this was a chronologically more drawn-out event

limits: No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence. The supplementary tables and figures (S1–S7) were not supplied; the shoreline altitudes and cross-profile data could not be checked. Landform and shoreline identification is manual, with no inter-operator or blind check reported. Age models carry no reported sensitivity tests. Several dates are excluded as contamination, and the Kollsjömyran isolation rests on two dates. Sub-claims: the deglaciation age of c. 10,500 cal. BP and the isolation at 9800 cal. BP are estimate_with_resolution (uncertainties only partly stated); the HS gradient of 2.75 m/10 km is regularity_in_range (±3 m, 60 km baseline); the Bonäs shoreline is excluded. The trigger mechanism (stochastic high water) is a proposal, untested. Inference: the paper contains internal inconsistencies (Figure 13b caption names 'Kroksjömyran' and gives the Heden coordinates; the Appendix cites Figure 14d for the Heden age model), suggesting unchecked figure references.

disagreements.target: Halden (1929, 1933, 1936): delayed deglaciation with stagnant basin ice
disagreements.support: Radiocarbon dates, varve counts and cited OSL ages put Orsasjön deglaciation at c. 10,500 cal. BP, consistent with continued 350 m/yr retreat.
disagreements.quote: There is therefore no evidence of a ‘delayed’ deglaciation and the dwelling of a stagnated ice mass in the Siljan Basin

disagreements.target: Halden (1936): interconnected ice-lateral lakes and their shoreline indicators
disagreements.support: The DSMs show the supposed shoreline indicators are ice-marginal drainage channels, and the local ice-dammed lakes were topographically separate.
disagreements.quote: are in fact ice-marginal drainage channels

disagreements.target: Halden (1936): HS marks at 215–219 m in the Skattungen–Oresjön basins
disagreements.support: No such marks are visible in that altitude interval on the DSMs, and a sediment threshold would have blocked Baltic water.
disagreements.quote: such cannot be distinguished in this altitude interval on the DSMs of this area

disagreements.support: HS indicators vary by metres over short distances, so isobase directions cannot be fixed from sparse data.
disagreements.quote: We think this is an overinterpretation of sparse data.

disagreements.target: von Post (1934): HS gradient of about 9 m per 10 km
disagreements.support: A fit to 37 mapped HS sites gives 2.75 m/10 km, matching Halden's 2.8 m/10 km.

disagreements.target: Nordell (1984a, 1984b): stagnant ice in the Orsasjön Basin
disagreements.support: The same deglaciation chronology as against Halden.
disagreements.quote: and also to some extent by Nordell (1984a, 1984b) for the Orsasjön Basin

disagreements.target: Norrman (1971) and Nordell (1984b): ice-marginal terraces in the Ockran–Born Valley
disagreements.support: The lower braid-plain level extends across the whole valley and was later split by erosion.
disagreements.quote: very unlikely to have been deposited – as suggested by Norrman (1971) and Nordell (1984b)

disagreements.target: Common assumption that Siljan isolation occurred during the Ancylus Lake stage
disagreements.support: The Kollsjömyran isolation dates place the isolation at c. 9800 cal. BP, in the Initial Littorina Sea stage.
disagreements.quote: it has often been assumed that the isolation of the Siljan Basin occurred during this Baltic Sea stage

disagreements.target: von Post (1934): catastrophic Åkerö drainage at the Littorina maximum
disagreements.support: The Heden and Åkerö chronologies place the rerouting at 8800–8500 cal. BP, unfolding over about 300 years.
disagreements.quote: we see a more plausible, slower-acting scenario for this event

disagreements.target: von Post (1934), De Geer (1910a), Högbom (1913, 1923), Wenner & Lannerbro (1952): Bonäs Line as palaeo-shoreline
disagreements.support: Dune-foot altitudes vary by more than 7 m over less than 300 m, and the regression gradient would imply an impossible lake level at Leksand.
disagreements.quote: being formed as an erosional feature cutting into distal Mora Delta sediment, as argued by von Post (1934)
